course_description:
Ever wondered how archaeologists know where to dig? Or why they dig square holes? And what they do with their finds once they leave the field? This course answers these questions and more. You'll be introduced to the fundamentals of doing archaeology, from fieldwork to lab work, covering a broad range of methods and techniques used to understand the human past across the world. Throughout, we'll also explore the ethics of archaeological practice, our responsibilities to local and Traditional Owner communities and the public, and other best-practice principles.

By the end of semester, you'll have the basic knowledge, skills and understanding needed to:

Course Structure

ARCS1001 runs across all 13 teaching weeks of semester. Each week pairs a 1.5-hour lecture with a 2-hour practical class held at either the Archaeology Teaching and Research Centre (ATARC) or in the Archaeology Teaching Laboratory (Michie Building, Room 325). The lectures will introduce the theory and method of key areas of archaeological practice, while the practicals will explore these areas further through applied activities and integrated problem-based learning exercises. This gives you the chance to put what you've learned into immediate, hands-on practice.

Cultural Sensitivities

Lectures and practicals in ARCS1001 include images of deceased people and the handling of replica casts of human bones. No actual human remains are used in this course. We recognise cultural sensitivities around this content and encourage you to contact the Course Coordinator if you have any concerns.

Course Communication

All course communication will be via Blackboard announcements and your student email, so please check both regularly. If you'd like to meet the Course Coordinator outside class times, please email me ( a.crowther@uq.edu.au ) to arrange an appointment.

Further Study

In conjunction with ARCA1000 Discovering Archaeology , ARCS1001 provides a foundation for several 2nd and 3rd level courses in archaeology, including ARCS2003 Forensics , ARCS2011 Lithics, ARCA2050 Historical Archaeology , ARCS2060 Field School, ARCS2070 Bioarchaeology , ARCS2080 Plants and Archaeology , ARCS2090 Animals and Archaeology , and ARCS3010 Field Archaeology .

course_aims: The main objectives of ARCS1001 are:

learning_outcomes.description: Show a familiarity with major themes, case studies and concepts in contemporary archaeological research at an introductory level.
Demonstrate a basic and general understanding of the practical methods and techniques of archaeological investigation.
Describe and demonstrate basic skills in archaeological analysis and interpretation.
Successfully demonstrate problem solving skills in archaeology
Successfully demonstrate critical analysis and writing skills.

assessment_details.title: Site Card
assessment_details.task_description: This assessment requires you to prepare a formal site recording package for a mock archaeological site modelled on the standard used by Australian cultural heritage practitioners. The site record will include: A completed site card , recording the location, environmental context, site description, condition, material components, etc. of a mock archaeological site as well as relevant photographs and artefact records. GIS maps showing site location, site extent, and other required spatial outputs. A written statement addressing the site's significance and recommendations regarding further work or management actions. The Site Card will be completed and submitted using the Inspera Assessment platform via a link in the Assessments folder in Blackboard. Guidelines on how to complete the Site Card as well as relevant background information will be provided. Find more information about using Inspera Assessment from the Library website , which provides the latest information for students about using Inspera. To see what the interface looks like, please try out the Inspera demonstration test here . This shows you the assessment interface using some test questions. Remember, Inspera is a university wide-platform, so there may be some question types in the demo that are not relevant to your discipline. To complete the assessment, you will require access to laptop/desktop computer that meets the device requirements for Inspera assessments. It is important that you check that your laptop meets the device requirements for using the Inspera Assessment platform. If you do not own a suitable laptop, you can borrow one from the Library or book use of a desktop computer in the library . Marking criteria: Criteria including rubrics are available in the ‘Assessments’ folder on the course Blackboard site. AI Use: This task has been designed to be challenging, authentic and complex. Whilst students may use AI technologies, successful completion of assessment in this course will require students to critically engage in specific contexts and tasks for which AI may provide limited support and guidance. A failure to reference AI use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct Policy. Students may be required to complete an AI usage declaration and submit it with their assessment. Additional resources are available through UQ AI Student Hub . assessment_details.submission_guidelines:
This assessment item must be submitted via Inspera on Blackboard Ultra.
Refer to the eLearning Guides for steps on how to submit your assignment. No emailed assessments will be accepted. Students must obtain proof of submission (such as a screenshot) of their assessment.
Students must abide by the Student Code of Conduct Policy which outlines that all submitted assessment must be their own work, except where properly referenced.
If you are experiencing technical difficulties with Blackboard or Inspera, please contact the ITS Support Team .
Deferral or extension
You may be able to apply for an extension .
The maximum extension allowed is 28 days. Extensions are given in multiples of 24 hours.
A request for an extension must be submitted as soon as it becomes evident that an extension is needed, and no later than the assessment due date and time. Please refer to the my.UQ Applying for an assessment extension page for information.
Extension requests are processed by the School of Social Science Administration Team. Course Coordinators are unable to grant extensions directly. Extensions in your final semester of study could delay your graduation to the next graduation period.
Late Extension Applications
Late applications must include supporting documentation outlining how it was impossible, or unsafe, for you to have applied by the due date and time. The School of Social Science will not accept personal statements.
Late submission
A penalty of 10% of the maximum possible mark will be deducted per 24 hours from time submission is due for up to 7 days. After 7 days, you will receive a mark of 0.
Assessments will not be accepted if it is more than one week (7 calendar days) late without prior approval.

learning_activities.topic: Week 1 Lecture: Course Introduction Overview of course aims, structure and assessment; introduction to the practical dimensions of archaeology Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03

Week 1 Practical: Fieldwork Safety and Mapping Mapping exercise at the ATARC. This is an outdoor activity so please wear closed-in shoes, long pants, a long-sleeved shirt and a hat. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Week 2 Lecture: Finding Sites Archaeological survey and site prospection Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Week 2 Practical: Survey Survey exercise at the ATARC. This is an outdoor activity so please wear closed-in shoes, long pants, a long-sleeved shirt and a hat. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Week 3 Lecture: Spatial Analysis in Archaeology Principles of spatial analysis including mapping and GIS Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03

Week 3 Practical: GIS (ONLINE) Introduction to mapping and spatial analysis using QGIS [Note: Owing to the EKKA holiday, there is no in-person practical class this week; you will be required to complete a self-directed learning activity on GIS] Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Week 4 Lecture: Archaeological Excavation The diversity and application of archaeological excavation techniques. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03

Week 4 Practical: Excavation Simulation excavation at the ATARC. This is an outdoor activity so please wear closed-in shoes, long pants, a long-sleeved shirt and a hat. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Week 5 Lecture: Geoarchaeology Soils, sediments and stratigraphy in archaeology and the importance of understanding site formation processes. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Week 5 Practical: Sediments and Stratigraphy Basic methods of analysing, describing and recording sediments and stratigraphy. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Week 6 Lecture: Understanding Chronology Constructing chronologies through relative and absolute dating methods. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Week 6 Practical: Chronology Relative and absolute dating methods in archaeology including radiocarbon calibration Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Week 7 Lecture: Stone Technologies Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Week 7 Practical: Stone Technologies Recognising and identifying stone tools; raw materials; technology and typology. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Week 8 Lecture: Ceramics, Glass and Metal Analysis and interpretation of ceramics, glass and metal objects in archaeology. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03

Week 8 Practical: Ceramics, Glass and Metal Methods of analysing, recording and describing ceramics, glass and metal objects; manufacturing methods, materials, styles. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Week 9 Lecture: Archaeobotany Using ancient plant remains to understand the human past. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Week 9 Practical: Archaeobotany Identification and analysis of different types of plant remains. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Mid-semester break - No Class
Week 10 Lecture: Zooarchaeology The archaeology of animals remains; methods, interpretation and significance. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Week 10 Practical: Zooarchaeology Identification and analysis of faunal remains. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
Week 11 Lecture: Curation and Data Management in Archaeology Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Week 11 Practical: In-Class Exam 90 minute in-class exam during your normal practical/lab time. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05
Week 12 Lecture: Bioarchaeology Human skeletal evidence in archaeology Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03
Week 12 Lab: Bioarchaeology Basic human skeletal anatomy; recognising different palaeopathological conditions; human evolution Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04

Week 13 Lecture: Communicating Archaeology to the Broader Audience Hear from a panel of museum and outreach experts on the importance of communicating archaeological research to different audiences Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03

Week 13 Practical: Museum tours Tours of the UQ Anthropology and Antiquities museums hosted by their curatorial teams including a behind the scenes peek at their collections Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04
